purpose: R3 quant gate (P002 B3, configs/eval/gates.yaml quant_vs_parent.fp8): Qwen3.5-2B FP8 (ModelOpt PTQ, per-tensor, calib 128, through the app node) vs its bf16 parent, paired on the same OCRBench questions, same vLLM engine settings

models.candidate_fp8: outputs/graph/runs/n3-beaf85b927870c8d/ptq/quantized (quant_method modelopt; vision + lm_head kept bf16; research)

benchmark.name: OCRBench
benchmark.citation: Liu et al., OCRBench: On the Hidden Mystery of OCR in Large Multimodal Models, Science China Information Sciences 2024 (arXiv:2305.07895)
benchmark.comparability: measured in this app (vLLM, no thinking, 500-question subset): NOT comparable with model-card OCRBench numbers; only the paired FP8 - bf16 delta is the gate number

engine.driver: scripts/qa/ocrbench_vllm_gate.py (compare refuses pairs whose engine settings differ other than quantization)

gate.rule: fp8: mean delta >= -1 PASS, [-2, -1) WARN, < -2 or any benchmark < -5 FAIL; WARN uncertain_run_full if CI low < -2

speed_note: load 206.5 s (bf16) vs 233.2 s (fp8); generate 500 questions 230.1 / 193.4 s (bf16 a/b) vs 223.3 s (fp8), enforce_eager on a shared GB10: no FP8 speed-up measured here; a CUDA-graph latency benchmark is a separate item (bench R3)
caveats: vLLM batched greedy is not bit-reproducible run to run: two identical bf16 runs differ on 3/500 answers (-0.2 points); the FP8 delta (-0.6) is within about 3x that noise and its CI contains 0
one benchmark only (OCRBench subset); the P002 forgetting check on general benchmarks is not part of this gate yet
single quantization run (calib 128); calibration sensitivity not measured for 2B
